name: Iron Man
tagline: The armored pioneer of the Marvel Cinematic Universe
biography: Anthony Edward 'Tony' Stark was an eccentric industrialist who inherited Stark Industries from his father Howard Stark. After being ambushed and captured by the Ten Rings terrorist group in Afghanistan, Stark suffered shrapnel injuries near his heart. Refusing to build missiles for his captors, he forged an electromagnetic chest arc reactor and the rudimentary Mark I armor with Dr. Ho Yinsen. Returning to Malibu, he refined the technology into high-altitude powered suits, shut down Stark Industries' weapons manufacturing, and publicly announced 'I am Iron Man.' Stark became a core architect of the Avengers, facing extraterrestrial threats and technological perils across the globe.
powers: Genius-level intellect and engineering mastery
Armor-enabled supersonic flight and maneuverability
Repulsor beam projection from palms and chest Unibeam
Micro-missile salvos and nanotech weapon morphing
Enhanced physical durability and superhuman strength
equipment: Mark I through Mark LXXXV Armor Suites (including Mark L and LXXXV Nanotech suits)
spoilerBio: In 2023, Stark engineered the quantum GPS enabling the Time Heist and fabricated the Nano Gauntlet. Facing Thanos during the Battle of Earth, Stark wrested the Infinity Stones into his Mark LXXXV armor, declaring 'I am Iron Man' to disintegrate Thanos and his armies, sacrificing his life to save the cosmos.
spoilerWarning: Contains character death spoilers for Avengers: Endgame

name: Thor
tagline: Asgardian god of thunder and founding Avenger
biography: Thor Odinson is the Asgardian God of Thunder and son of King Odin Borson and Queen Frigga. Initially arrogant and eager for war against the Frost Giants, Thor was stripped of his divine abilities and cast down to Earth as a mortal until he proved himself worthy to wield the enchanted hammer Mjolnir. Learning humility, selflessness, and valor, Thor became a founding cornerstone of the Avengers, wielding thunder, lightning, and divine strength to defend Midgard and the Nine Realms.
powers: Godlike superhuman physical strength, stamina, and longevity
Atmospheric electrokinesis and weather control
Dimensional traversal via the Bifrost Bridge
Flight propulsion through Mjolnir and Stormbreaker
Electrified energy projection without external foci
equipment: Asgardian royal armor and crimson cloak

teamMemberships.role: Transient Cosmic Guest ('Asgardians of the Galaxy')

spoilerBio: Across his journey, Thor endured the destruction of Asgard during Ragnarok, followed by the execution of his brother Loki and half his people by Thanos in Infinity War. Channeling his grief into the forged king's weapon Stormbreaker, Thor struck Thanos in the chest but failed to stop the Snap. After decapitating a retired Thanos in 2018, Thor fell into severe depression in New Asgard. Rejoining the Avengers for the Time Heist, an unworthy-feeling Thor re-summoned Mjolnir from 2013 and fought alongside Cap and Iron Man in the Battle of Earth. Later, after fighting with the Guardians, Thor reunited with a cancer-stricken Jane Foster (the Mighty Thor) to defeat Gorr the God Butcher, adopting Gorr's resurrected daughter Love as his own.
spoilerWarning: Contains major plot spoilers for Thor: Ragnarok, Avengers: Infinity War, Avengers: Endgame, and Thor: Love and Thunder

name: Captain America
aliases: The Star-Spangled Man with a Plan
tagline: The First Avenger and moral compass of Earth's Mightiest Heroes
biography: Steven Grant Rogers was an impoverished Brooklyn art student rejected repeatedly from WWII military service due to chronic health issues. Dr. Abraham Erskine recognized his profound moral resolve, selecting him for the Project Rebirth Super Soldier program. Transformed into peak human perfection, Rogers led the Howling Commandos behind enemy lines to dismantle Johann Schmidt's HYDRA operations. Plunging a Valkyrie bomber into Arctic ice to save millions, Rogers awoke 66 years later in the 21st century to lead the Avengers against global and extraterrestrial crises.

Mastery of master-level hand-to-hand martial combat and shield aerodynamics
Accelerated cellular healing and immunity to terrestrial intoxicants
Supreme battlefield tactics and inspirational leadership
Demonstrated worthiness to summon and wield Mjolnir
equipment: Indestructible Vibranium disc shield forged by Howard Stark

Choosing to remain in the 1940s with Peggy Carter, an elderly Rogers returned to 2023 to formally pass his vibranium shield and the mantle of Captain America to Sam Wilson.

name: Spider-Man
tagline: Queens' friendly neighborhood wall-crawler and junior Avenger
biography: Peter Benjamin Parker was an orphaned Queens high school student living with his Aunt May who gained arachnid abilities after being bitten by a radioactive spider. Operating secretly as a local crimefighter, he was recruited by Tony Stark during the Avengers' clash over the Sokovia Accords. Equipped with high-tech Stark suits, Parker halted Adrian Toomes' scavenged weapons network and joined the Avengers on Titan and Earth against Thanos.

Superhuman proportionate spider strength and agility

Acrobatic equilibrium and heightened kinetic perception

Peter suffered the devastating death of Aunt May at the hands of the Green Goblin, but rallied with two multiversal Spider-Men to cure their enemies. To avert catastrophic incursion, Peter asked Strange to cast a spell erasing all memory of Peter Parker from existence, starting anew in solitary anonymity.

name: Star-Lord
aliases: Leader of the Guardians of the Galaxy
tagline: The mixtape-loving leader of the Guardians of the Galaxy
biography: Peter Jason Quill was born in Missouri to human Meredith Quill and the cosmic Celestial entity Ego. Following his mother's tragic passing from brain cancer in 1988, eight-year-old Peter was abducted into space by Yondu Udonta and the Ravagers. Rather than delivering him to Ego, Yondu raised Quill as a scavenger and thief. Adopting his mother's pet name 'Star-Lord', Quill stole an orb containing the Power Stone on Morag, triggering a cascade of events that united him with Gamora, Drax, Rocket, and Groot. As captain of the Milano, Quill transformed his found family of eccentric outlaws into the premier guardians of cosmic peace.

name: Spider-Man
tagline: The definitive Columbia Pictures trilogy web-slinger
biography: Peter Parker was a shy, bookish Midtown High student raised by his Uncle Ben and Aunt May in Forest Hills, Queens. During a high school field trip to Columbia University, he was bitten by a genetically designed super-spider, manifesting superhuman reflexes, sticky fingertips, and organic spinnerets inside his wrists. Initially chasing prize money as 'The Human Spider' in an underground wrestling ring, Peter neglected to stop an armed robber who minutes later murdered Uncle Ben. Haunted by Ben's words—'With great power comes great responsibility'—Peter committed his life to protecting New York City. Later pulled into the MCU through Doctor Strange's destabilized spell, he aided his younger counterpart variants in curing his old adversaries.

Superhuman proportionate arachnid strength, agility, and reflexes
Wall-crawling surface adhesion through micro-structures

name: Spider-Man
tagline: The brilliant Oscorp skateboarder and acrobatic protector of Manhattan
biography: Peter Parker was an inquisitive science student abandoned by his parents, geneticist Richard Parker and Mary Parker, under mysterious circumstances. Uncovering his father's old briefcase led Peter directly into Oscorp, where he snuck into the biocable laboratory and was bitten by a genetically altered arachnid. Leveraging his father's decay rate algorithm, Peter designed high-tensile mechanical web-shooters using Oscorp biocable. After a burglar shot Uncle Ben, Peter embraced heroic purpose as Spider-Man, defending New York from the Lizard and Oscorp's creations.

Dynamic acrobatic agility and proportionate spider strength
Hyper-reactive spider-sense precognition
Scientific genius in biochemistry and electrical engineering

spoilerBio: At the top of the Manhattan clock tower in The Amazing Spider-Man 2, Peter battled Harry Osborn's Green Goblin. Although Peter defeated Osborn, Gwen Stacy fell down the tower; Peter's web caught her a fraction of a second too late, and the whiplash snapped her neck, plunging Peter into grief and vengeful darkness. Pulled across dimensions to the MCU in No Way Home, Peter found profound emotional redemption when he dove from the Statue of Liberty to catch a falling MJ, successfully saving her and letting go of his self-directed bitterness.
spoilerWarning: Contains major character death spoilers for The Amazing Spider-Man 2 (2014) and Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021)

name: Spider-Man
tagline: Brooklyn's teenage Spider-Man charting his own heroic rhythm
biography: Miles Morales was an artistic Brooklyn high schooler attending Visions Academy whose life changed when bitten in an abandoned subway station by an interdimensional spider from Earth-42. Witnessing the tragic death of his universe's Peter Parker at the hands of Kingpin, Miles promised to disable the Super-Collider. Mentored by an out-of-shape Peter B. Parker from Earth-616 and bonding with Gwen Stacy, Miles embraced his leap of faith to become Brooklyn's new Spider-Man. In Across the Spider-Verse, Miles learned from Miguel O'Hara that his origin violated the multiverse's canon events, sparking an intense rebellion to save both his father and the fabric of reality.

name: Spider-Gwen
tagline: The rhythm-driven web-warrior of Earth-65
biography: Hailing from Earth-65, teenager Gwen Stacy was bitten by a radioactive spider, becoming Spider-Woman while playing drums in The Mary Janes rock band. When her universe's Peter Parker transformed into the Lizard to defend himself against bullies and died in her arms, her father Captain George Stacy led a citywide manhunt against her. Sucked through Kingpin's collider into Earth-1610, Gwen formed an indelible bond with Miles Morales. Later recruited into Miguel O'Hara's elite multiversal Spider-Society, Gwen ultimately chose to break ranks to assemble her own band of spider-allies to rescue Miles.

tagline: The relentless architect and protector of multiversal canon events
biography: Miguel O'Hara is a brilliant geneticist from Nueva York on Earth-928 who spliced his DNA with spider genes. Unlike most spider-heroes, Miguel possesses retractable talons, fangs that secrete non-lethal paralytic venom, and red laser webs, while lacking organic wall-adhesion and a conventional spider-sense. After attempting to replace a deceased alternate version of himself and inadvertently causing an entire universe's unraveling, Miguel founded the multiversal Spider-Society at the Citadel to ruthlessly protect predetermined canon events across realities.

name: Wolverine
tagline: The adamantium-clawed mutant survivor who defined superhero cinema
biography: Born in 19th-century Canada as James Howlett, Logan discovered his mutation when bone claws erupted from his hands in childhood. Possessing an accelerated cellular healing factor and heightened animalistic senses, Logan survived centuries of battlefield combat across the Civil War, World War I, World War II, and Vietnam alongside his half-brother Victor Creed. Recruited into Col. William Stryker's Team X, Logan was later subjected to the Weapon X program, fusing unbreakable molten adamantium to his skeletal frame. Joining Charles Xavier's X-Men, Logan became the fierce protector of mutantkind.
powers: Accelerated regenerative cellular healing factor
Six retractable razor-sharp bone claws coated in indestructible adamantium
Indestructible adamantium-bonded skeleton
Superhuman animalistic olfactory, auditory, and visual tracking senses
Longevity and decades of lethal hand-to-hand combat mastery
spoilerBio: In 2006 on Alcatraz, Logan was forced to euthanize the woman he loved, Jean Grey, when her unchecked Dark Phoenix persona threatened to incinerate the island. In 2029, with his mutant healing factor poisoned by decades of adamantium toxicity, Logan fought to escort young Laura (X-23) and mutant youth refugees to safety across the Canadian border. In an exhausting final battle against Donald Pierce's Reavers and his savage genetic clone X-24, Logan was impaled on a tree limb and died peacefully holding Laura's hand.
spoilerWarning: Contains character death and plot spoilers for X-Men: The Last Stand (2006) and Logan (2017)

name: Wolverine (Worst Variant)
tagline: The grieving alternate Wolverine who redeemed his fallen world alongside Deadpool
biography: This alternate Logan hailed from an alternate timeline where his fellow X-Men were slaughtered while he was drinking at a local bar. Overwhelmed by survivor's guilt, Logan donned his yellow-and-blue uniform in bitter penance and fell into drunken despair. Pulled across the multiverse by Wade Wilson to serve as an anchor being for Earth-10005, Logan was cast into the Void by rogue TVA agent Mr. Paradox, where he joined forces with the Void resistance to overthrow Cassandra Nova.
spoilerBio: In the climax of Deadpool & Wolverine, Logan finally forgave himself for failing his original team. Donning his iconic cowl, he joined hands with Deadpool across the unstable matter-antimatter core of the Time Ripper, withstanding the cosmic energy load to destroy the device, preserve the timeline, and find a renewed home with Wade's family.

name: Professor X
tagline: The telepathic visionary fighting for human-mutant coexistence
biography: Professor Charles Francis Xavier was an exceptionally powerful mutant telepath who dedicated his life and inherited Westchester fortune to establishing Xavier's School for Gifted Youngsters. Believing passionately that mutants and humans can peacefully share the Earth, Xavier created the X-Men to defend both species against human bigotry and mutant extremism. Utilizing Cerebro, a spherical neural amplifier, Xavier could track mutant signatures globally. Despite enduring paralysis, government hostility, and the devastation of Sentinel timelines, Xavier's unwavering optimism guided generations of mutant heroes.

spoilerBio: In the dystopian future of 2029, a nonagenarian Xavier suffered from a degenerative brain disease causing catastrophic psychic seizures that previously harmed mutants in Westchester. Cared for in an abandoned smelting plant on the Mexican border by Logan and Caliban, Charles regained his lucidity before being tragically murdered in his bed by X-24, Logan's feral genetic clone.

name: Professor X (Earth-838)
tagline: The compassionate telepathic chairman of Earth-838's Illuminati
biography: Charles Xavier of Earth-838 was the revered telepathic leader and chairman of the Illuminati, governing alongside Reed Richards, Black Bolt, Captain Carter, Maria Rambeau, and Karl Mordo. Championing compassion and moral restraint, Xavier presided over multiversal threats and utilized a floating yellow hoverchair. When Doctor Strange was apprehended after traversing dimensions with America Chavez, Xavier advocated for reason over summary execution.
spoilerBio: When a Darkhold-corrupted Scarlet Witch infiltrated the Illuminati headquarters, Xavier entered her subconscious in an effort to rescue the real Wanda Maximoff trapped beneath the mental rubble. However, the entity's chaos magic overwhelmed him, brutally snapping his neck inside the psychic plane and terminating his life.

name: Professor X (Young)
tagline: The young Oxford scholar who built the first class of X-Men
biography: Charles Xavier in his youth was a brilliant, charismatic Oxford graduate in genetics who grew up in Westchester alongside his foster sister Raven Darkhölme. In 1962, CIA agent Moira MacTaggert recruited Xavier to investigate Sebastian Shaw's Hellfire Club during the Cuban Missile Crisis. Partnering with Erik Lehnsherr, Charles recruited young mutants to create the original First Class of X-Men. When a deflected bullet severed Charles' spine during the missile standoff on the Cuban beach, his divergent worldview from Magneto cemented their tragic rift. Charles persevered through personal despair, learning in Days of Future Past to channel hope rather than fear.

name: Magneto
tagline: The Master of Magnetism championing mutant survival at all costs
biography: Erik Magnus Lehnsherr survived the horrors of the Auschwitz concentration camp in WWII, where the trauma of losing his parents triggered his catastrophic mutant mastery over magnetic fields. Hardened by humanity's propensity for systematic genocide, Erik came to believe that the burgeoning mutant race (Homo superior) could never safely coexist with Homo sapiens. As Magneto, he forged the militant Brotherhood of Mutants, utilizing metal manipulation to weaponize everything from the Golden Gate Bridge to tactical nuclear missiles. Despite his ruthless methods, Magneto shared an unbreakable bond of mutual respect with Charles Xavier, repeatedly uniting with the X-Men when total extinction threatened their kind.

name: Magneto (Young)
tagline: The vengeful Nazi hunter who forged the Brotherhood's identity
biography: Following WWII, a young Erik Lehnsherr hunted escaped Nazi war criminals across the globe to avenge his mother's murder by Sebastian Shaw (Klaus Schmidt). In 1962, Charles Xavier pulled him from the ocean when Erik attempted to drag down Shaw's submarine with his magnetism alone. Charles helped Erik discover that true magnetic power lies between rage and serenity. After executing Shaw with a slow-moving Nazi coin through the brain, Erik seized Shaw's telepathy-blocking helmet and parted ways with Charles. Across the alternate 1973 timeline and the rise of Apocalypse, Erik oscillated between destructive vengeance and profound grief.
powers: Raw magnetic field generation capable of lifting naval battleships and soccer stadiums
Metal manipulation down to the microscopic iron traces in human blood
Magnetic flight and concussive kinetic blasts

name: Deadpool
tagline: The fourth-wall-shattering mercenary who rescued the multiverse
biography: Wade Winston Wilson was a dishonorably discharged Special Forces operative working as a mercenary in New York City. Diagnosed with terminal cancer, Wade submitted to Ajax (Francis Freeman) in the underground Weapon X workshop. Injected with mutant serum and subjected to oxygen-deprivation torture, Wade unlocked a hyper-accelerated cellular regenerative healing factor that cured his disease but left his skin severely scarred. Adopting the persona Deadpool, Wade paired lethal katanas with fourth-wall-breaking commentary. Recruited by the TVA to save his timeline, Wade traversed the multiverse to team with a reluctant Wolverine variant.

name: Weapon XI / Wade Wilson
tagline: Col. Stryker's mutant-killer experiment with a mouth sewn shut
biography: Wade Wilson was initially a wisecracking mercenary operative in Major William Stryker's clandestine mutant Team X in 1973. Possessing master swordsmanship and superhuman reflexes to deflect automatic gunfire, Wade later left the unit. Captured by Stryker, he was subjected to the Weapon XI program at Three Mile Island, having his mouth surgically sealed and genetic abilities from multiple captured mutants grafted into his DNA, including Scott Summers' optic blasts, John Wraith's teleportation, and Logan's healing factor.
spoilerBio: Controlled remotely via a computer terminal by Stryker to eliminate Wolverine, Weapon XI battled Logan and Victor Creed atop a nuclear cooling tower before being decapitated by Logan's adamantium claws. In Deadpool 2's post-credits sequence, a time-traveling Deadpool from the modern timeline traveled back to 1979 and shot Weapon XI repeatedly in the head to erase him from continuity.

name: Mister Fantastic
tagline: The hyper-elastic scientific patriarch of the Fantastic Four
biography: Dr. Reed Richards was an ambitious polymath and theoretical physicist who funded an expedition into deep space to study cosmic radiation cloud patterns. When the cloud arrived early, Richards and his crew—Sue Storm, Johnny Storm, Ben Grimm, and Victor von Doom—were irradiated. Returning to Earth, Richards discovered his molecular structure had mutated, permitting him to stretch, deform, expand, and compress his body into nearly any geometric configuration. Establishing the Baxter Building as their headquarters, Reed balanced groundbreaking physics with public heroism, neutralizing Victor's metallic menace and later teaming with the Silver Surfer to divert Galactus.

Accompanying Reed's cosmic cloud space station mission, Sue was inundated by cosmic radiation that unlocked the ability to manipulate light waves around her body to render herself invisible, as well as project invisible psionic force fields capable of stopping speeding trucks and redirecting thermal blasts. Balancing her affection for Reed with Victor von Doom's corporate advances, Sue proved to be the formidable emotional and tactical anchor of the Fantastic Four.

Exposed to cosmic rays, Johnny developed the power to envelop his body in fiery plasma without harming himself, project devastating flame bursts, and take flight by manipulating air currents. Flamboyant and loving the spotlight, Johnny coined the team's hero names and uniforms. In 2024, an alternate version of this Johnny Storm resurfaced in the Void under Cassandra Nova's rule in Deadpool & Wolverine, where his mouth got him in legendary trouble with the Merc with a Mouth.

When the cosmic ray cloud struck the station while Ben was on an exterior spacewalk, his physiology was completely transmuted into a massive, orange, rock-like dermal armor. Possessing immense superhuman strength, Ben struggled with his public monstrous appearance before embracing his heroic identity, famous for his battle cry: 'It's Clobberin' Time!'

Financing Reed's space station exploration in exchange for majority profit rights, Victor was caught in the cosmic ray cloud after a shielding breach. Unlike his companions whose changes were immediate, Victor's body slowly ossified into organic metallic alloy while gaining the power to absorb, channel, and discharge high-voltage electricity. Blaming Reed for his company's bankruptcy and his physical condition, Doom donned a traditional Latverian metal mask and green hooded cloak, seeking vengeance on the Fantastic Four.

spoilerWarning: Contains character death spoilers for Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness

name: Blade
tagline: The legendary vampire-hunting Daywalker
biography: Eric Brooks was born after his pregnant mother was bitten by the vampire Deacon Frost in 1967, resulting in a hybrid physiology possessing all of a vampire's superhuman physical strengths, enhanced senses, and agility, without any vulnerability to sunlight, garlic, or silver—earning him the fearful title of 'The Daywalker.' Raised and armed by master armorer Abraham Whistler, Blade utilized an arsenal of customized silver weaponry, UV light explosives, and titanium swords to wage an unrelenting war against vampire syndicates. In 2024, Blade was discovered surviving in the Void in Deadpool & Wolverine, affirming to Wade that 'there's only ever gonna be one Blade.'
powers: Superhuman physical strength, agility, reflexes, and durability
Complete immunity to sunlight, vampire bites, and garlic
Accelerated cellular healing from vampire physiology
Mastery of martial arts, sword combat, and firearms marksmanship
equipment: Titanium-edged broadsword with concealed handle security trap
Custom silver-tipped stakes and double-barreled shotgun
UV flash grenades and garlic essence darts
Black leather trenchcoat and ballistic sunglasses

sources.title: New Line Cinema Blade Official Production Records

name: Venom
tagline: The chaotic investigative journalist and alien symbiote duo
biography: Eddie Brock was a dogged San Francisco investigative journalist whose career imploded when he confronted Life Foundation CEO Carlton Drake with stolen classified documents. Investigating Drake's human trials involving extraterrestrial symbiotes, Brock was bonded with the alien symbiote Venom. Despite initial terror, Brock and Venom formed an idiosyncratic symbiotic partnership, developing a shared palate for bad guys and tater tots. Together they defeated Riot, Carnage (Cletus Kasady), and multiversal incursions, briefly visiting the MCU timeline during Doctor Strange's spell before leaving a drop of symbiote behind.
powers: Gigantic superhuman physical strength capable of lifting cars and stopping trains
Fluid shape-shifting, tendril generation, and web-like swinging lines
Accelerated biological healing from gunshot wounds and broken bones
Fanged jaws and predatory sensory tracking

name: Green Goblin
tagline: The manic, glider-riding arch-nemesis of Spider-Man
biography: Dr. Norman Osborn was the brilliant, cutthroat founder and CEO of Oscorp Technologies. Facing the loss of crucial military contracts and imminent board dismissal, Osborn tested an unstable chemical performance enhancer on himself. The formula drastically augmented his physical strength, reflexes, and intelligence while fracturing his psyche, giving birth to the sadistic Green Goblin alter ego. Equipped with the high-speed Goblin Glider and an arsenal of explosive pumpkin bombs, Osborn terrorized New York City as Spider-Man's most personal and dangerous nemesis.
powers: Superhuman physical strength, durability, agility, and reflexes
Genius-level intellect in advanced weaponry and cybernetics
Unpredictable psychological warfare and manipulation
equipment: High-speed rocket-propelled Goblin Glider armed with twin machine guns and blades
Thermite pumpkin bombs and razor bats
Armored emerald flight suit and menacing goblin battle mask

relationships.relation: Multiversal Target & Tragic Victim ('Gods don't have to choose')

sources.title: Marvel.com Green Goblin Norman Osborn Profile

spoilerBio: During his final rooftop duel with Tobey Maguire's Spider-Man in 2002, Osborn attempted a sneak attack with his remote glider, but Peter dodged, causing the glider to fatally impale Osborn. Pulled across the multiverse into the MCU just moments before his death in No Way Home, Osborn broke his goblin mask and sought help from Peter Parker, but the Goblin persona reasserted control, murdering Aunt May with his glider. At the Statue of Liberty, Holland's Peter was stopped from killing Osborn by Maguire's Spider-Man, and Osborn was injected with a cure that permanently restored his sanity before returning home.
spoilerWarning: Contains climactic plot and character death spoilers for Spider-Man (2002) and Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021)

name: Doctor Octopus
aliases: The Power of the Sun in the Palm of My Hand
tagline: The four-tentacled fusion scientist who conquered his artificial mind
biography: Dr. Otto Octavius was a brilliant, compassionate nuclear scientist sponsored by Oscorp to achieve sustainable self-sustaining fusion power. To manipulate the volatile fusion core safely, Octavius developed four artificial-intelligence-assisted titanium mechanical tentacles fused to his spine, protected by a neural inhibitory chip. When his demonstration destabilized into a miniature runaway sun, the energy surge fried his inhibitor chip, allowing the tentacles' artificial intelligence to corrupt his mind and compel him to rebuild the reactor at any cost.
powers: Four highly articulate, super-strong titanium mechanical tentacles
Tentacle-enabled wall-scaling, heavy lifting, and rapid locomotion
Peerless nuclear physicist intellect
equipment: Spinal-mounted four-tentacle cybernetic harness with gripping pincers
Neural inhibitor chip (restored with Stark nanotech)

relationships.relation: Revered Protégé turned Adversary turned Saved Friend
Savior who engineered the replacement inhibitor chip

spoilerBio: In the climax of Spider-Man 2, Peter Parker unmasked himself and broke through the tentacles' neural override, inspiring Octavius to reassert conscious control. Overcoming the AI, Octavius sacrificed his life by dragging the runaway fusion machine into the Hudson River to save New York City. Pulled into the MCU moments prior to drowning, Doc Ock was freed from the tentacles' corruption when Peter fabricated a replacement neural inhibitor chip, allowing Octavius to ally with the three Spider-Men in the final battle.
spoilerWarning: Contains climactic plot and sacrifice spoilers for Spider-Man 2 (2004) and Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021)

name: Electro
tagline: The living electrical lightning storm seeking recognition
biography: Maxwell 'Max' Dillon was a chronically overlooked and underappreciated electrical engineer at Oscorp who idolized Spider-Man after the hero saved his life in traffic. On his birthday, while attempting to repair a power cable over an Oscorp bio-electric vat, Dillon was electrocuted and fell into a holding tank of genetically modified electric eels. The incident mutated his cellular matrix into pure electrical current. Misunderstood and feeling betrayed when police attacked him in Times Square, Electro turned his devastating high-voltage power against Spider-Man and the city's power grid.
powers: Pure electrical manipulation, lightning projection, and electro-magnetism
Conversion into electrical current enabling instantaneous wire transmission
Power absorption from municipal electrical grids and Arc Reactor energy
equipment: Stark Arc Reactor (briefly affixed to his chest harness in No Way Home)

relationships.relation: Former Idol turned Adversary turned Reconciled Companion

sources.title: Sony Pictures The Amazing Spider-Man 2 Notes

spoilerBio: At the climax of The Amazing Spider-Man 2, Spider-Man and Gwen Stacy overloaded Dillon with power from the Ravenswood electrical grid, causing Electro's body to explode. Pulled into the MCU prior to his death in No Way Home, Dillon discovered that the new dimension's grid granted him a yellow, stabilized electrical charge. Siphoning energy from an arc reactor, Electro battled the Spider-Men until Andrew Garfield and Doc Ock removed the reactor and cured him, restoring Dillon to ordinary human form.
spoilerWarning: Contains climactic plot spoilers for The Amazing Spider-Man 2 (2014) and Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021)

name: Doctor Strange
tagline: Master of the Mystic Arts guarding the multiverse against catastrophic incursions
biography: Dr. Stephen Vincent Strange was an acclaimed but egotistical New York neurosurgeon whose hands were shattered in a devastating car accident. When modern medicine failed, Strange traveled to Kamar-Taj in Nepal, where the Ancient One revealed the mystic arts and alternate dimensions. Dedicated to the discipline of sorcery, Strange became master of the New York Sanctum, warded off Dormammu with the Time Stone, and orchestrated the one victory path out of 14,000,605 possibilities against Thanos in Endgame. After accidentally puncturing reality during a spell for Peter Parker, Strange journeyed through the multiverse to protect America Chavez from a grief-stricken Wanda Maximoff.
powers: Mastery of the Mystic Arts (Eldritch light shields, Tao mandalas, and portal creation)
Dimensional traversal and astral projection
Chronokinesis (former wielder of the Time Stone / Eye of Agamotto)
Darkhold dreamwalking and third eye awakening
equipment: Cloak of Levitation (sentient relic granting flight and defense)
Sling Ring for dimensional gateway travel

name: Black Widow
tagline: The supreme S.H.I.E.L.D. agent and founding Avenger who wiped the red from her ledger
biography: Natasha Romanoff was taken as a young child into the Soviet Red Room academy, subjected to physiological augmentation and rigorous assassination training under General Dreykov. Sent on deadly missions, Romanoff's life changed when S.H.I.E.L.D. agent Clint Barton was sent to eliminate her but instead recruited her. Romanoff became Director Nick Fury's most trusted operative, went undercover at Stark Industries, and became a founding cornerstone of the Avengers.
powers: Master hand-to-hand martial artist (Sambo, Judo, Karate, and Krav Maga)
Master covert spy, interrogator, and multi-lingual infiltrator
Expert marksmanship and precision weapons handling

sources.title: Marvel.com Black Widow Natasha Romanoff Bio

spoilerBio: During the Time Heist in Endgame, Natasha and Clint traveled to Vormir. Discovering that obtaining the Soul Stone required the sacrifice of a loved one, Natasha fought Clint to ensure his survival, falling to her death from the cliff so the Avengers could restore the universe.
spoilerWarning: Contains character death spoilers for Avengers: Endgame

name: Hulk
tagline: The gamma-irradiated titan who fused brains with brawn
biography: Dr. Robert Bruce Banner was a renowned nuclear physicist who attempted to recreate Abraham Erskine's Super Soldier Serum using gamma radiation instead of Vita-Rays. When an experiment went awry, Banner shielded a colleague and absorbed a lethal dose of gamma rays, resulting in a cellular mutation that causes him to transform into the giant, rage-fueled Hulk whenever his heart rate spikes or emotions flare. Joining the Avengers, Banner spent years viewing the Hulk as a curse until retreating to a Mexican beach lab during the Blip, spending 18 months in a gamma chamber to merge Banner's genius intellect with the Hulk's physical invulnerability ('Smart Hulk').
powers: Virtually limitless superhuman strength scaling with emotional adrenaline
Near-absolute physical invulnerability and regenerative tissue repair
Colossal leaping capability crossing miles in a single bound
Genius-level intellect in nuclear physics, radiation, and quantum mechanics
equipment: Stretchy microfiber shorts and tactical glasses
Nano Gauntlet (wielded to resurrect the universe in Endgame)

sources.title: Marvel.com Hulk Bruce Banner Official Bio

spoilerBio: In 2023, during the Time Heist, Banner traveled to 2012 New York to convince the Ancient One to surrender the Time Stone. With his body capable of surviving immense gamma radiation, Banner donned the Nano Gauntlet in the Avengers Compound, snapping his fingers to resurrect everyone dusted by Thanos five years earlier, suffering permanent burns down his right arm in the process.
spoilerWarning: Contains climactic plot spoilers for Avengers: Endgame (2019)

name: Scarlet Witch
tagline: The mythical chaos-magic sorceress of devastating multiversal power
biography: Wanda Maximoff was a native of Sokovia who lost her parents to a Stark Industries mortar shell at age ten. Protesting foreign occupation, Wanda and her twin brother Pietro volunteered for Baron Wolfgang von Strucker's HYDRA experiments with Loki's scepter. The Mind Stone amplified her latent magical predisposition, granting her telekinesis, psionic energy projection, and telepathic hypnosis. Initially fighting the Avengers, the twins defected during the Battle of Sokovia. Wanda fell in love with Vision, but the trauma of losing him in Infinity War led her to rewrite Westview into a sitcom reality. Corrupted by the Darkhold, Wanda traversed dimensions seeking her children before ultimately bringing down Mount Wundagore to destroy the cursed text across the cosmos.
powers: Chaos Magic and spontaneous reality alteration
Telekinesis, flight, and psionic energy blast projection
Telepathy, mental persuasion, and nightmare inducement
Darkhold dreamwalking across multiversal bodies
equipment: The Darkhold (ancient grimoire of dark magic - destroyed)

teamMemberships.role: Avenger (Age of Ultron through Civil War)

appearances.title: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness

sources.title: Marvel.com Scarlet Witch Wanda Maximoff Cinematic Profile

spoilerBio: Corrupted by the Darkhold following the grief of losing Vision and Westview, Wanda dreamwalked across the multiverse to Earth-838 to seize America Chavez, ruthlessly eliminating the Illuminati. Confronted by the terror of her alternate children, Wanda broke the dark spell, using her chaos magic to crush Mount Wundagore and destroy every copy of the Darkhold across the cosmos.
spoilerWarning: Contains major antagonist and climax spoilers for Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness

name: Hawkeye
tagline: The peerless archer and grounding heart of the Avengers
biography: Clinton Francis Barton was an elite marksman recruited into S.H.I.E.L.D. by Director Nick Fury as one of the agency's primary tactical assets. Assigned to assassinate the Black Widow in Budapest, Barton defied orders to spare Romanoff, forging a legendary partnership. Armed with a customized recurve bow and a versatile quiver of high-tech trick arrows, Hawkeye became a founding member of the Avengers, fighting heroically in New York and Sokovia.
powers: Flawless peak-human marksmanship with bows, firearms, and thrown projectiles
Mastery of master-level hand-to-hand martial arts and swordsmanship (as Ronin)
Elite tactical reconnaissance and espionage
equipment: Custom carbon fiber collapsible recurve and compound bows
Quiver of custom trick arrows (Pym particle, explosive, acid, thermal, EMP, cable)
Ronin dual ninja katanas and armored tunic
spoilerBio: When his wife Laura and three children vanished during the Blip in 2018, overwhelming grief drove Barton to adopt the blood-soaked persona of Ronin, traveling the globe to butcher cartels and syndicates. In 2023, Natasha Romanoff found him in Tokyo to recruit him for the Time Heist. On Vormir, Barton fought desperately to sacrifice himself for the Soul Stone, but was forced to watch Romanoff sacrifice her life instead. Returning to the Battle of Earth, Barton guarded the Nano Gauntlet until the Snap brought his family safely home.
spoilerWarning: Contains major plot spoilers for Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame

name: Black Panther
tagline: The noble warrior king who shared Wakanda's wonders with the world
biography: T'Challa was the crown prince of the technologically peerless African kingdom of Wakanda. Following the tragic assassination of his father King T'Chaka at the Vienna UN conference, T'Challa ascended the throne, ingesting the sacred Heart-Shaped Herb to receive the superhuman blessings of the Panther Goddess Bast. Defending his birthright against his cousin Erik Killmonger, T'Challa was transformed by Killmonger's righteous grief over global oppression, choosing to abandon Wakanda's centuries-long isolationism to build international outreach centers. T'Challa led Wakanda's armies in defense of the universe during the Infinity War and Endgame before his untimely passing.
powers: Enhanced physical strength, speed, stamina, and agility granted by the Heart-Shaped Herb
Heightened senses and kinetic equilibrium
Supreme mastery of traditional Wakandan martial combat
Visionary diplomatic and political leadership

Retractable vibranium claws capable of scratching Captain America's shield
Kimoyo beads communication and medical interface

name: Black Panther / Shuri

tagline: Wakanda's chief technological prodigy who stepped into the mantle of the Panther
biography: Princess Shuri is the head of the Wakandan Design Group, renowned globally as one of the most brilliant scientific minds on Earth. Shuri revolutionized Wakanda's technological infrastructure, developing kinetic panther habits, silent sneakers, and remote piloting technology. Following the devastating deaths of her brother T'Challa and mother Queen Ramonda, Shuri wrestled with vengeance against Namor and the underwater kingdom of Talokan. Using a synthetic Heart-Shaped Herb she genetically engineered, Shuri gained the powers of Bast, becoming the new Black Panther while ultimately choosing mercy over cyclical bloodshed.
powers: Enhanced physical strength, speed, and agility from synthetic Heart-Shaped Herb
World-class genius in engineering, artificial intelligence, and vibranium physics
Wakandan martial arts and twin energy gauntlet combat

name: Captain Marvel
tagline: The photon-charged cosmic avenger safeguarding galaxies across the universe
biography: Carol Susan Jane Danvers was an elite US Air Force test pilot working on Dr. Wendy Lawson's (Mar-Vell) experimental light-speed engine. When Kree warrior Yon-Rogg attacked their aircraft, Danvers shot the engine to prevent it falling into enemy hands, absorbing the astronomical cosmic energies of the Tesseract (Space Stone). Amnesiac and indoctrinated as the Kree warrior 'Vers' on Hala, Carol was captured by Skrulls and crash-landed on Earth in 1995. Partnering with a young S.H.I.E.L.D. agent Nick Fury, Carol unlocked her suppressed memories, dismantled the Supreme Intelligence's control chip, and ignited her full Binary potential, inspiring Fury to draft the Avengers Initiative.
powers: Immense cosmic energy manipulation and devastating photon blast projection
FTL interstellar self-propelled flight and spatial survival
Cosmic-level physical strength, invulnerability, and radiant binary aura
Energy absorption and kinetic transmutation
equipment: Custom Starforce Kree battle suit retuned to Air Force red, blue, and gold
Interstellar pager modified by Nick Fury

name: Ant-Man
tagline: The reformed ex-con who unlocked the Quantum Realm and saved half the universe
biography: Scott Edward Harris Lang was an expert systems engineer who served three years in San Quentin after executing an ethical whistleblowing cyber-heist against his corrupt employer Vistacorp. Struggling to secure honest employment to support his young daughter Cassie, Lang was drawn into a staged burglary at Dr. Hank Pym's residence, discovering the Ant-Man suit. Chosen by Pym to succeed him, Lang mastered Pym Particle shrinking and ant telepathy to defeat Darren Cross. Trapped in the Quantum Realm during Thanos' snap, Lang emerged five hours later (five Earth years) with the crucial quantum time travel theory that allowed the Avengers to execute the Time Heist.
powers: Size alteration: shrinking to subatomic quantum scale or expanding to 65-foot Giant-Man
Concentrated physical kinetic density when shrunken
Telepathic insect control through electromagnetic EMP communication nodes
Acrobatic close-quarters combat

Red (shrinking) and Blue (enlarging) Pym Particle throwing discs

name: Winter Soldier / Bucky
tagline: The Howling Commando survivor who broke free from seventy years of mind control
biography: James Buchanan 'Bucky' Barnes was Steve Rogers' loyal childhood companion who enlisted in the 107th Infantry during WWII. Captured by HYDRA in Austrian territory, Barnes was subjected to early biological enhancement by Arnim Zola before Captain America liberated him. Reunited as Howling Commandos, Barnes fell from a speeding munitions train in the Alps and was recovered by Soviet HYDRA operatives. Fitted with a cybernetic titanium arm and subjected to cryostasis and memory-erasing mental trigger codes, Barnes became the legendary assassin 'The Winter Soldier.' Steve Rogers helped him remember his humanity, and Shuri later cured his trigger words in Wakanda.
powers: Super-Soldier enhanced physical strength, agility, reflexes, and healing
Vibranium cybernetic arm equipped with internal kinetic dampening and extreme crushing force
Mastery of master-level knife combat, hand-to-hand martial arts, and military firearms

Tactical combat knives and assault rifles

name: Captain America / Falcon
tagline: The high-flying pararescue airman who accepted the shield of Captain America
biography: Samuel Thomas Wilson was a former United States Air Force Pararescue airman who operated the experimental EXO-7 Falcon flight harness during tactical night missions. Following the loss of his wingman Riley, Wilson worked as a VA counselor in Washington D.C., where he befriended Steve Rogers. When HYDRA compromised S.H.I.E.L.D., Wilson donned his Falcon wings to aid Rogers in taking down Project Insight. Wilson became a devoted Avenger, took Steve's side in the Civil War, and fought Thanos' forces in Infinity War and Endgame.
powers: Exceptional aerial dogfighting agility and combat maneuvering
Peak human military martial combat and shield-throwing trajectory calculations
Inspirational leadership, empathy, and diplomatic mediation
equipment: Vibranium Captain America Shield handed down by Steve Rogers
Wakandan vibranium flight suit with articulate wings and thrusters

spoilerBio: Following the Battle of Earth in Endgame, an elderly Steve Rogers passed his original circular vibranium shield to Wilson. Initially donating the shield to the Smithsonian due to the complex racial history of America, Wilson reclaimed it after John Walker disgraced the mantle, formally flying into action as the new Captain America in a custom Wakandan vibranium flight suit.
spoilerWarning: Contains major plot spoilers for Avengers: Endgame and The Falcon and the Winter Soldier

name: Loki
tagline: The God of Mischief whose path from conqueror to savior bound the multiverse
biography: Loki Laufeyson was the biological son of King Laufey of Jotunheim, adopted as an abandoned infant by King Odin of Asgard and raised alongside Thor. Learning in adulthood of his Frost Giant heritage, Loki's feelings of inferiority and betrayal exploded into a succession of schemes: attempting to destroy Jotunheim, leading a Chitauri invasion of New York City for the Tesseract, and seizing the Asgardian throne under Odin's guise before fighting alongside his brother during the defense of Asgard against Hela.
powers: Mastery of Asgardian sorcery, astral projections, duplicates, and illusions
Telekinesis, energy blast projection, and shape-shifting
Time-slipping across past, present, and alternate realities
Frost Giant physiology granting physical strength and cold immunity
equipment: Chitauri Scepter housing the Mind Stone (former)
spoilerBio: Defying Thanos in Infinity War, the original Loki was choked to death aboard the Statesman. A 2012 variant escaped with the Tesseract to the TVA, learned compassion and selflessness, and ultimately sacrificed his personal freedom at the End of Time, weaving the dying multiversal branches together with his bare hands to become the God of Stories.
spoilerWarning: Contains climax spoilers for Loki Season 2 and Infinity War

name: Nick Fury
tagline: The mastermind director of S.H.I.E.L.D. who brought together the Avengers
biography: Nicholas Joseph Fury was a decorated Cold War CIA officer who rose through the ranks of the Strategic Homeland Intervention, Enforcement and Logistics Division (S.H.I.E.L.D.) to become its legendary Director. In 1995, an encounter with Carol Danvers and the alien Skrulls convinced Fury that humanity was woefully unprepared for extraterrestrial threats, prompting him to create the Avengers Initiative. Working from the shadows, Fury brought together Iron Man, Captain America, Thor, Hulk, Black Widow, and Hawkeye when Loki invaded Earth. Surviving HYDRA's assassination attempt in Washington D.C., Fury continued running covert operations across the cosmos.
powers: Master strategist, spymaster, and psychological interrogator
Expert military tactician and firearms marksmanship
Network of clandestine safehouses, covert resources, and global contacts
equipment: S.H.I.E.L.D. high-tech black trenchcoat with stealth armor lining
Intergalactic transmitter pager connected to Captain Marvel

sources.title: Marvel.com Nick Fury Official Cinematic Bio

name: Storm
tagline: The weather-wielding mutant leader and teacher at Xavier's School
biography: Ororo Munroe is an Omega-level mutant born with the ability to psionically manipulate atmospheric weather patterns. Recruited by Charles Xavier into the X-Men, Ororo became a central teacher and field leader at the Xavier Institute. Capable of generating hurricane winds, lightning bolts, and blizzard temperatures at will, Storm remained an unflinching protector of both young mutants and peaceful coexistence, eventually succeeding Xavier as the operational head of the school.
powers: Psionic atmospheric and meteorological weather control
Generation of lightning bolts, tornadoes, blizzards, and fog banks
Atmospheric thermal flight via wind currents
Immunity to extreme environmental weather extremes
equipment: Custom X-Men tactical leather combat suit with flowing cape attached to wrists

sources.title: Marvel.com Storm Ororo Munroe Character Profile

name: Jean Grey / Phoenix
tagline: The Class 5 telekinetic mutant carrying the devastating Phoenix force
biography: Dr. Jean Grey was an accomplished geneticist, physician, and senior member of the X-Men. Possessing Class 5 telepathy and telekinesis, Jean's boundless psionic potential was guarded by mental blocks installed by Charles Xavier in childhood to shield her sanity. Working from the Xavier Institute, Jean served as the emotional and scientific core of the team, treating injured students and standing alongside Cyclops, Storm, and Professor X in advocating for peaceful mutant coexistence.
powers: Class 5 molecular telekinesis capable of disintegrating matter at an atomic level
Vast psionic telepathy and mind reading
Telekinetic flight and spherical force shields
equipment: Custom medical and tactical X-Men suits
spoilerBio: In the climax of X2: X-Men United, Jean sacrificed her life holding back millions of gallons of water from the breached Alkali Lake dam to allow the X-Jet to escape. Re-emerging in X-Men: The Last Stand as the unrestrained, omnipotent Phoenix, her destructive split persona killed Scott Summers and disintegrated Charles Xavier. During the Battle of Alcatraz, Jean briefly regained conscious control and pleaded with Logan to end her life, dying at his claws to stop the catastrophe.
spoilerWarning: Contains major character death spoilers for X2 and X-Men: The Last Stand

name: Cyclops
tagline: The disciplined field commander and optic-blast anchor of the X-Men
biography: Scott Summers was Charles Xavier's first student and the steadfast field commander of the X-Men. Scott's mutation produces continuous, uncontrollable beams of red concussive force from his eyes, which can only be held in check by ruby-quartz lenses and his specialized battle visor. Dedicated to Xavier's dream of human-mutant harmony, Cyclops led the X-Men against Magneto's Brotherhood on Liberty Island and William Stryker at Alkali Lake, standing as the tactical backbone of the team.
powers: Continuous concussive optic force blasts from eyes
Spatial awareness and geometric bank-shot calculation
Mastery of small-unit tactical leadership and martial arts
equipment: Custom ruby-quartz tactical visor with manual and side-control aperture sliders
Ruby-quartz sunglasses for daily civilian safety
spoilerBio: Grief-stricken following Jean Grey's apparent death at Alkali Lake, Scott was haunted by telepathic whispers calling him back to the spillway. Arriving at Alkali Lake in X-Men: The Last Stand, Scott discovered the resurrected Jean, whose emerging Dark Phoenix persona overwhelmed him in an embrace that disintegrated his body, leaving behind only his floating ruby-quartz glasses.
spoilerWarning: Contains character death spoilers for X-Men: The Last Stand (2006)

name: Gamora
aliases: The Deadliest Woman in the Galaxy
tagline: Former assassin raised by Thanos who forged a new family with the Guardians of the Galaxy
biography: A Zehoberei survivor whose homeworld was halved by Thanos, Gamora was raised and cybernetically augmented by the Mad Titan to become his deadliest warrior. Tasked with retrieving the Orb on Xandar, she defected alongside Peter Quill, Rocket, Groot, and Drax to keep the Power Stone out of Ronan's hands, becoming a foundational Guardian of the Galaxy.
spoilerBio: In Avengers: Infinity War, Thanos forced Gamora to reveal the Soul Stone's location on Vormir and threw her to her death from the cliff to claim it. Following the 2023 Time Heist, an alternate 2014 variant of Gamora remained in the main timeline, though she never shared the original Gamora's history with the Guardians.
spoilerWarning: Contains character death spoilers for Avengers: Infinity War (2018)
powers: Cybernetically enhanced strength, speed, and durability
Master swordsmanship and hand-to-hand martial arts
Accelerated healing and high-altitude resilience

name: Drax the Destroyer
tagline: Literal-minded Kylosian warrior fueled by vengeance and fierce loyalty to the Guardians
biography: After Ronan the Accuser murdered his wife Ovette and daughter Kamaria under Thanos's orders, Drax carved a path of destruction across the galaxy seeking retribution. Imprisoned in the Kyln, he reluctantly joined Peter Quill, Gamora, Rocket, and Groot, discovering a second family among the Guardians of the Galaxy.
spoilerBio: In Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3, Drax helped liberate hundreds of imprisoned Star Children from the High Evolutionary's Arête Laboratories. Realizing his true calling was as a father rather than a destroyer, Drax remained on Knowhere alongside Nebula to raise the rescued children.
spoilerWarning: Contains ending plot spoilers for Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 (2023)

Master dual-blade close-quarters combatant
Extreme pain tolerance

name: Rocket Raccoon
tagline: Cybernetically engineered tactical genius, weapons expert, and Guardian of the Galaxy
biography: Created on Counter-Earth by the High Evolutionary through painful cybernetic and genetic experimentation, Rocket escaped his creator and survived as a bounty hunter alongside Groot. After a Kyln prison break united him with Star-Lord, Gamora, and Drax, Rocket became the Guardians' premier tactician, pilot, and heavy-weapons engineer.
spoilerBio: When the Blip wiped out his teammates, Rocket remained on Earth for five years, collaborating with the Avengers on the Time Heist. In Guardians Vol. 3, after barely surviving a near-fatal attack by Adam Warlock, Rocket confronted the High Evolutionary, rescued the captive test animals, and succeeded Peter Quill as Captain of the new Guardians of the Galaxy.
spoilerWarning: Contains major plot spoilers for Avengers: Endgame and Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3

Master starship pilot and battlefield tactician
Enhanced animalistic agility and acute hearing

name: Groot
tagline: Original Flora colossus and founding Guardian who gave his life shielding his friends on Xandar
biography: A sentient tree-like Flora colossus from Planet X, the original Groot traveled the cosmos as Rocket's loyal partner and protector. Despite speaking only the phrase 'I am Groot', his companions understood the nuanced emotional intent behind his words as he fought alongside Star-Lord, Gamora, Drax, and Rocket to defend Xandar from Ronan the Accuser.
spoilerBio: During the Battle of Xandar in Guardians of the Galaxy (2014), Groot sacrificed his life by wrapping the Guardians in a protective sphere of branches ('We are Groot') as the Dark Aster crashed. Rocket planted a surviving twig from his remains, giving life to Groot's son.
spoilerWarning: Contains character sacrifice spoilers for Guardians of the Galaxy (2014)
powers: Elastic limb growth, wooden shield generation, and vine entanglement
Superhuman strength and regenerative healing
Bioluminescent spore projection

name: Nebula
tagline: Cybernetically rebuilt Luphomoid assassin who overcame Thanos's torture to defend the galaxy
biography: Raised alongside Gamora as Thanos's adoptive daughter, Nebula was repeatedly mutilated and rebuilt with cybernetic parts whenever she lost sparring matches to her sister. Initially serving Ronan the Accuser, Nebula later reconciled with Gamora on Ego's planet and turned her vengeance toward destroying Thanos.
spoilerBio: Surviving the Blip alongside Rocket, Nebula fought alongside the Avengers in the Time Heist, where she shot and killed her own loyalist 2014 past self to protect Clint Barton and Gamora. Following the Battle of Earth, she became a core Guardian and ultimately remained on Knowhere to lead its peaceful reconstruction.
spoilerWarning: Contains major plot spoilers for Avengers: Endgame and Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3
powers: Extensive cybernetic strength, durability, and self-repairing nanotech limbs
Master assassin and weapons combatant
Built-in cybernetic memory projection and hacking interfaces

name: Mantis
tagline: Empathic Guardian capable of sensing and pacifying emotions—even those of a Celestial
biography: Raised in isolation on Ego's living planet to soothe the Celestial's restless mind with her empathic touch, Mantis initially knew little of the outside universe. When the Guardians arrived, she risked Ego's wrath to warn Drax and Gamora of his true plans, earning a permanent place in the Guardians of the Galaxy.
spoilerBio: In Guardians Vol. 3, having already been revealed as Ego's biological daughter and Peter Quill's half-sister, Mantis helped defeat the High Evolutionary and tamed three ferocious Abilisks. Feeling she had spent her entire life serving others' wishes, she departed the team with the Abilisks to discover her own identity.
spoilerWarning: Contains ending plot spoilers for Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 (2023)
powers: Touch-based empathic sensing and emotional manipulation
Ability to induce sleep in powerful beings, including Ego and Thanos
Enhanced agility and martial arts proficiency

name: Yondu Udonta
tagline: Centaurian Ravager captain and Peter Quill's true adoptive father figure
biography: Leader of an exiled Ravager clan, Yondu Udonta was hired by Ego in 1988 to abduct eight-year-old Peter Quill from Earth. Upon discovering Ego's lethal fate for his offspring, Yondu defied his employer and raised Peter aboard the Eclector, teaching him thievery and survival while hiding deep paternal affection.
spoilerBio: After Taserface staged a mutiny aboard the Eclector, Yondu escaped with Rocket and Groot and flew to Ego's planet to rescue Quill. In the film's climax, Yondu gave Peter the sole remaining Aero-Rig space suit, sacrificing his life in the vacuum of space ('He may have been your father, boy, but he wasn't your daddy') and earning a full Ravager funeral.
spoilerWarning: Contains character death spoilers for Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 (2017)
powers: Mastery of whistle-guided telekinetic arrow trajectories
Seasoned starship captain and close-quarters brawler

name: Thanos
tagline: Genocidal Titan warlord obsessed with rebalancing the cosmos using all six Infinity Stones
biography: A powerful warlord from the ruined planet Titan, Thanos became convinced that unchecked population growth doomed every civilization to extinction. Commanding the Black Order and Chitauri armies, he orchestrated proxy invasions for the Infinity Stones before embarking on a personal crusade to assemble the completed Infinity Gauntlet.
spoilerBio: In Infinity War, Thanos killed Loki, sacrificed Gamora on Vormir, overpowered the Avengers on Titan and in Wakanda, and snapped away half of all life in the universe. After destroying the Stones on the Garden so his work could never be undone, he was ambushed and decapitated by Thor in the opening weeks of Avengers: Endgame.
spoilerWarning: Contains major plot and death spoilers for Avengers: Infinity War and Endgame
powers: Immense superhuman strength, durability, and hand-to-hand combat mastery
Genius-level military strategist
Cosmic omnipotence when wielding the six Infinity Stones

name: Hela
tagline: Odin's banished firstborn daughter who draws unstoppable power from Asgard itself
biography: Once Odin's fierce executioner who helped conquer the Nine Realms, Hela's unquenchable bloodlust led Odin to imprison her in Hel for millennia. Released upon Odin's passing, she shattered Thor's enchanted hammer Mjolnir with a single hand and reclaimed Asgard's throne with an undead army.
spoilerBio: Realizing Hela's strength grew infinitely as long as Asgard existed, Thor and Loki orchestrated Ragnarok by placing Surtur's crown into the Eternal Flame. As Thor evacuated the Asgardian people aboard the Statesman, the resurrected fire giant Surtur plunged his Twilight Sword into Asgard, obliterating Hela along with the realm.
spoilerWarning: Contains ending spoilers for Thor: Ragnarok (2017)
powers: Asgardian godlike strength, reflexes, and near-invulnerability
Infinite manifestation of razor-sharp necroswords and blades
Necromancy via the Eternal Flame

name: Erik Killmonger
tagline: Exiled Wakandan prince and black-ops veteran who challenged the throne to arm the oppressed
biography: Born in Oakland as N'Jadaka, son of Wakandan prince N'Jobu, Erik grew up orphaned after King T'Chaka killed his father for betraying Wakanda's secrecy. Excelling at MIT and as a US Navy SEAL black-ops assassin, Killmonger returned to Wakanda to claim the throne by ritual combat and distribute vibranium weaponry worldwide.
spoilerBio: In the climax of Black Panther, T'Challa defeated Killmonger on the Wakandan vibranium maglev tracks using sonic stabilizers to disrupt his Golden Jaguar habit. Refusing medical imprisonment, Killmonger asked to watch the sunset over Wakanda before pulling out the spear blade, choosing death over bondage. He later appeared to Shuri in the Ancestral Plane in Wakanda Forever.
spoilerWarning: Contains character death and sequel cameo spoilers for Black Panther and Wakanda Forever
powers: Peak human combat conditioning enhanced by the Heart-Shaped Herb
Elite tactical strategist and military marksman

name: Vulture
tagline: Working-class salvage contractor turned black-market Chitauri weapons dealer
biography: After Damage Control forced his salvage crew off the 2012 Battle of New York cleanup site, Adrian Toomes retained salvaged Chitauri technology to provide for his family. Working alongside Phineas Mason, Toomes engineered a winged flight harness and spent eight years discreetly selling alien-hybrid weapons across the East Coast until Spider-Man intervened.
spoilerBio: Deduceing Peter Parker's secret identity as his daughter Liz's prom date, Toomes threatened Peter to stay out of his final Avengers cargo plane heist. After Spider-Man rescued Toomes from an exploding Chitauri power core and left him for the authorities, Toomes showed gratitude in prison by refusing to reveal Spider-Man's identity to Mac Gargan.
spoilerWarning: Contains ending plot spoilers for Spider-Man: Homecoming (2017)
powers: Experienced aerial combatant and black-market strategist
equipment: Chitauri-powered winged Exo-Suit with talon boots

name: Mysterio
tagline: Former Stark hologram engineer who weaponized illusion drones to pose as Earth's new hero
biography: Dismissed as unstable by Tony Stark after creating the B.A.R.F. holographic system, Quentin Beck united fellow disgruntled Stark Industries alumni to fabricate the persona of Mysterio—a supposed multiversal hero battling Elemental monsters. Using hundreds of weaponized Stark illusion drones, Beck manipulated Peter Parker into handing over the E.D.I.T.H. satellite network.
spoilerBio: During the London Tower Bridge battle in Far From Home, Peter Parker mastered his 'Peter Tingle' spider-sense to fight blind through Beck's lethal illusions and reclaim E.D.I.T.H. Fatally wounded by a ricocheting drone shot, Beck died—but his team doctored battle footage and leaked it to TheDailyBugle.net, framing Spider-Man for murder and exposing Peter Parker's identity to the world.
spoilerWarning: Contains character death and identity reveal spoilers for Spider-Man: Far From Home (2019)
powers: Master illusionist and psychological manipulator
Expert engineer of holographic drone combat choreography
equipment: Motion-capture illusion suit with fishbowl helmet

name: Shang-Chi
tagline: Master martial artist who confronted his father's Ten Rings empire to protect the mystic realm of Ta Lo
biography: Trained from childhood as an elite assassin by his immortal father Xu Wenwu, Shang-Chi fled the Ten Rings organization as a teenager to live quietly in San Francisco under the name 'Shaun'. When Wenwu's assassins ambushed him for his mother's pendant, Shang-Chi traveled to the hidden village of Ta Lo alongside his sister Xialing and friend Katy.
spoilerBio: In Ta Lo, Shang-Chi mastered his mother's wind-based martial arts. After Wenwu realized he had been deceived by the Dweller-in-Darkness, he sacrificed himself and passed the mystic Ten Rings to Shang-Chi, who rode the Great Protector dragon to destroy the soul-eating creature. Afterward, Wong summoned Shang-Chi to Kamar-Taj to investigate the Rings' mysterious beacon alongside Bruce Banner and Carol Danvers.
spoilerWarning: Contains ending and post-credits spoilers for Shang-Chi (2021)
powers: Peak human martial arts mastery across multiple disciplines
Ta Lo mystical wind and chi manipulation
Immortality, energy projection, and kinetic force control via the Ten Rings

name: Yelena Belova
tagline: Red Room-trained assassin freed from mind control who fights alongside the Thunderbolts*
biography: Raised in a covert 1990s Ohio sleeper cell alongside Natasha Romanoff, Alexei Shostakov, and Melina Vostokoff, Yelena Belova was subjected to General Dreykov's chemical mind control in the Red Room. Freed by an antidote vial, Yelena tracked down Natasha in Budapest and teamed with her surrogate family to bring down the airborne Red Room Fortress.
spoilerBio: After Natasha Romanoff's death in Endgame, Yelena worked as a covert operative before being caught in Valentina Allegra de Fontaine's O.X.E. vault trap alongside Bucky Barnes, U.S. Agent, Ghost, and Red Guardian, ultimately forming the Thunderbolts* / New Avengers.
spoilerWarning: Contains plot spoilers for Black Widow (2021) and Thunderbolts* (2025)
powers: Master Red Room martial artist, acrobat, and espionage infiltrator
Expert marksman and close-quarters knife combatant
equipment: Tactical vest with concealed utility pockets

sources.title: Marvel.com Yelena Belova On Screen Profile

name: Namor
tagline: Mutant ruler of underwater Talokan blessed with winged ankles and vibranium-forged might
biography: Born in 1571 after his pregnant mother ingested a vibranium-mutated underwater herb, Ch'ah Toh Almehen became a mutant endowed with winged ankles, aquatic breathing, and centuries-long youth. Revered as K'uk'ulkan by his hidden underwater kingdom of Talokan, Namor aggressively protected his people's vibranium from surface-world exploitation, sparking a fierce war with Wakanda.
spoilerBio: After slaying Queen Ramonda in a retaliatory flood of Birnin Zana, Namor battled the new Black Panther, Shuri, in an arid desert arena that dehydrated his aquatic strength. Choosing mercy over execution, Shuri offered an honorable yield, forging a fragile peace and tactical alliance between Talokan and Wakanda.
spoilerWarning: Contains major plot spoilers for Black Panther: Wakanda Forever (2022)
powers: Mutant flight via ankle wings
Superhuman strength rivaling Hulk-tier adversaries while hydrated
Amphibious physiology and extreme longevity
equipment: Gold and jade Talokanil royal headdress and armor

name: Okoye
tagline: Unwavering General of Wakanda's Dora Milaje royal guard and Midnight Angel warrior
biography: Commander of Wakanda's elite all-female Dora Milaje, Okoye served as King T'Challa's chief military strategist and protector. Fiercely devoted to the Wakandan throne, she fought alongside the Avengers against Thanos's Outriders in Infinity War and during the Battle of Earth in Endgame.
spoilerBio: During Wakanda Forever, after Talokanil warriors abducted Shuri and Riri Williams, Queen Ramonda stripped Okoye of her General rank. Redeemed when Shuri gifted her an experimental vibranium Midnight Angel suit, Okoye rescued Everett Ross and helped defend Wakanda alongside the Dora Milaje.
spoilerWarning: Contains plot spoilers for Black Panther: Wakanda Forever (2022)
powers: Master vibranium spear fighting and close-quarters combat
Peak tactical battlefield command

name: Vision
tagline: Mind Stone-powered vibranium synthezoid born from J.A.R.V.I.S. and Ultron's cradle
biography: Forged by Ultron inside Helen Cho's Regeneration Cradle from cellular vibranium and the Mind Stone, Vision was awakened when Tony Stark and Bruce Banner uploaded the J.A.R.V.I.S. AI and Thor struck the cradle with lightning. Proving worthy to lift Mjolnir, Vision joined the Avengers and formed a profound romantic bond with Wanda Maximoff.
spoilerBio: In Avengers: Infinity War, to prevent Thanos from completing the Infinity Gauntlet, Vision urged Wanda to destroy the Mind Stone inside his forehead. Though Wanda shattered the stone and killed him, Thanos used the Time Stone to rewind Vision's death and tear the Mind Stone from his skull, killing him a second time.
spoilerWarning: Contains character death spoilers for Avengers: Infinity War (2018)
powers: Intangibility and molecular density manipulation
Solar energy beam projection from the Mind Stone
Flight, superhuman strength, and synthetic intellect

name: Wong
tagline: Steadfast Master of the Mystic Arts, guardian of Kamar-Taj, and Earth's Sorcerer Supreme
biography: Dedicated librarian and Master of the Mystic Arts at Kamar-Taj, Wong guarded the Ancient One's forbidden texts and fought alongside Stephen Strange against Kaecilius and Dormammu. During the Battle of Earth, Wong opened mystic Sling Ring portals across the cosmos to assemble every resurrected hero against Thanos.
spoilerBio: Because Stephen Strange was dusted during the five-year Blip, Wong legitimately inherited the mantle of Earth's Sorcerer Supreme, later leading Kamar-Taj's defense against the Darkhold-corrupted Scarlet Witch in Multiverse of Madness.
spoilerWarning: Contains plot spoilers for Spider-Man: No Way Home and Multiverse of Madness
powers: Mastery of Eldritch Magic shields, whips, and portals
Encyclopedic knowledge of multiversal sorcery and artifacts
