name: Rogue
tagline: Runaway mutant whose skin contact absorbs others' life force, memories, and mutant powers
biography: After accidentally putting her boyfriend into a coma with her first kiss, Marie fled Mississippi and encountered Logan in the Canadian wilderness. Rescued from Magneto's Brotherhood on Liberty Island, Rogue enrolled at Xavier's School for Gifted Youngsters, forming a close romance with Bobby Drake while struggling with the isolation of her lethal touch.
spoilerBio: In X-Men: The Last Stand, yearning for normal human intimacy with Bobby, Rogue voluntarily lined up to receive Worthington Labs' mutant 'cure', temporarily neutralizing her mutation so she could hold Bobby's hand without harming him.
spoilerWarning: Contains plot spoilers for X-Men: The Last Stand (2006)
powers: Involuntary life-force, memory, and mutant ability absorption through skin contact
equipment: Full-coverage leather gloves and X-Men flight uniform

name: Nightcrawler
tagline: Devout, acrobatic mutant teleporter who infiltrated the White House under Stryker's control
biography: A gentle, deeply religious former Munich circus acrobat marked by indigo skin, yellow eyes, and a prehensile tail, Kurt Wagner was brainwashed by William Stryker into attacking the US President. Rescued and cleared by Storm and Jean Grey in Boston, Nightcrawler joined the X-Men's Alkali Lake rescue mission.
spoilerBio: During the Alkali Lake climax of X2, Nightcrawler risked fatal collision by teleporting blindly through solid walls into Stryker's underground Cerebro chamber alongside Storm, freeing Professor Xavier just in time to save both mutants and humans worldwide.
spoilerWarning: Contains climax spoilers for X2: X-Men United (2003)
powers: Instantaneous line-of-sight teleportation with sulfurous smoke burst
Wall-crawling adhesion and prehensile tail dexterity
Peak acrobatic agility

name: Iceman
tagline: Cryokinetic X-Men student who froze Pyro in combat and mastered full organic ice armor
biography: An early student at Xavier's Institute who befriended Rogue upon her arrival, Bobby Drake struggled with his family's rejection after coming out as a mutant in Boston. Rising from student to full X-Men field combatant, Bobby faced off against former classmate Pyro during the Battle of Alcatraz, unlocking his full organic ice form.
spoilerBio: In the dystopian 2023 future of Days of Future Past, Iceman died fighting adaptive Sentinels to buy time for Kitty Pryde and Wolverine's time-travel mission. Once Logan altered 1973 history, Bobby was restored alive and well at the peaceful Westchester school.
spoilerWarning: Contains timeline death and restoration spoilers for Days of Future Past (2014)
powers: Cryokinesis and sub-zero thermal manipulation
Full-body organic ice armor transformation
Creation of ice walls and shields

name: Beast (Young)
tagline: Mutant prodigy biochemist who built Cerebro and the X-Jet while embracing his bestial form
biography: A teenage genius recruited by CIA agent Moira MacTaggert and Charles Xavier in 1962, Hank McCoy designed the original Cerebro helmet, X-Men flight suits, and the Blackbird SR-71 jet. Attempting to suppress his prehensile feet with Mystique's DNA, Hank accidentally triggered his blue-furred, super-strong Beast transformation, becoming Xavier's steadfast deputy.
spoilerBio: In Dark Phoenix, devastated when Jean Grey accidentally killed Mystique, Hank briefly defected to Magneto's Genosha faction seeking vengeance. Recognizing Jean's innocence during the train ambush, Hank reconciled with Xavier and succeeded him as headmaster of the Jean Grey School for Gifted Youngsters.
spoilerWarning: Contains plot spoilers for Dark Phoenix (2019)
powers: Superhuman strength, claw dexterity, and acrobatic leaps
Genius-level biochemistry, aeronautics, and engineering intellect

name: Quicksilver
tagline: Supersonic mutant speedster who broke Magneto out of the Pentagon and saved the X-Mansion
biography: Living in his mother's basement in Washington D.C. in 1973, teenage speedster Peter Maximoff was recruited by Logan and Charles Xavier to break Erik Lehnsherr out of a plastic cell deep beneath the Pentagon. A decade later, searching for Erik—secretly his biological father—Peter arrived at the X-Mansion just in time to join the X-Men against Apocalypse.
spoilerBio: When Havok's energy blast detonated the X-Mansion's Blackbird hangar in X-Men: Apocalypse, Peter raced through the expanding fireball in microseconds, tossing every single student, teacher, and pet safely onto the front lawn before the building collapsed.
spoilerWarning: Contains set-piece spoilers for X-Men: Apocalypse (2016)
powers: Extreme supersonic speed, perception, and reaction time
Momentum-amplified kinetic strikes

name: Mystique (Young)
tagline: Shapeshifting mutant who evolved from Magneto's Brotherhood into field leader of the X-Men
biography: Raised from childhood as Charles Xavier's adoptive sister, Raven Darkhölme struggled to conceal her blue-skinned mutation until Magneto encouraged her to embrace 'mutant and proud'. Following the Cuban Missile Crisis, she joined the Brotherhood before halting Bolivar Trask's assassination in 1973, inspiring a new generation of X-Men as their reluctant field commander.
spoilerBio: In Dark Phoenix, while attempting to talk down a cosmic-power-destabilized Jean Grey in Red Hook, Raven was accidentally hurled onto broken wooden rafters by Jean's telekinetic surge, dying in Hank McCoy's arms.
spoilerWarning: Contains character death spoilers for Dark Phoenix (2019)
powers: Cellular-level shapeshifting into any human form and voice
Enhanced agility, martial combat skill, and decelerated aging

name: Mystique
tagline: Lethal shapeshifting Brotherhood infiltrator and Magneto's most trusted lieutenant
biography: Acting as Magneto's chief espionage operative and ruthless second-in-command in the original X-Men trilogy, Mystique used her flawless shapeshifting to impersonate Senator Kelly, infiltrate Stryker's Alkali Lake base, and sabotage Cerebro. Agile and deadly in hand-to-hand combat, she remained fiercely loyal to the Brotherhood of Mutants.
spoilerBio: In X-Men: The Last Stand, after Magneto rescued her from a prison transport convoy, Mystique dove in front of a mutant-cure dart fired at Erik. Stripped of her mutation and reverted to ordinary human form, she was coldly abandoned by Magneto ('You're not one of us anymore'), prompting her to reveal the Brotherhood's camp location to the US government.
spoilerWarning: Contains plot spoilers for X-Men: The Last Stand (2006)
powers: Instantaneous cellular shapeshifting and vocal mimicry
Expert martial artist and acrobatic marksman

name: Gamora (2014 Variant)
tagline: Alternate-2014 Gamora brought to 2023 who forged an independent path with the Ravagers
biography: Pulled from an alternate 2014 timeline prior to ever meeting the Guardians of the Galaxy, this Gamora was still serving as Thanos's reluctant assassin when her father intercepted the Avengers' Time Heist. Convinced by the 2023 Nebula that she would eventually betray Thanos, she turned against her 2014 past and later joined Stakar Ogord's Ravager clan.
spoilerBio: During the Battle of Earth in Endgame, 2014 Gamora fought alongside the Avengers against Thanos's forces before disappearing afterward. By Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3, she operated as a hardened Ravager mercenary, briefly assisting the Guardians on Counter-Earth to save Rocket while making clear to Peter Quill that she was not the woman he had lost.
spoilerWarning: Contains timeline variant spoilers for Avengers: Endgame and Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3
powers: Cybernetically enhanced strength, speed, and durability
Master swordsmanship and hand-to-hand martial arts

name: Groot (Young / Son)
tagline: Son of the original Groot raised by the Guardians from a potted sapling into a towering protector
biography: Grown from a surviving twig of the original Groot after the Battle of Xandar, this younger Groot is a distinct individual raised by Rocket and the Guardians of the Galaxy. Maturing from a mischievous potted sapling into a video-game-obsessed teenager and eventually a muscular brawler, he inherited his father's gentle heart and fierce devotion to his found family.
spoilerBio: In Avengers: Infinity War, Teen Groot severed his own left arm to bind the Uru pieces of Thor's axe Stormbreaker before being dusted in the Blip. Restored in Endgame, he fought in the Battle of Earth and later evolved into a massive multi-armed protector in Guardians Vol. 3, even speaking 'I love you guys' to the audience-understood family before defending Knowhere with Rocket's new Guardians.
spoilerWarning: Contains major plot spoilers for Avengers: Infinity War and Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3
powers: Elastic limb growth, wooden shield generation, and vine entanglement
Multi-armed combat transformation and spore illumination
Regenerative Flora colossus physiology

name: Thanos (2014 Variant)
tagline: Alternate-2014 Thanos who discovered the Time Heist and invaded 2023 Earth to remake the universe
biography: In an alternate 2014 timeline prior to assembling any Infinity Stones, Thanos discovered the Avengers' 2023 Time Heist when his daughter Nebula's cybernetic network entangled with her future self's memories. Witnessing his future victory and subsequent execution, this Thanos abandoned his original plan of halving life and vowed instead to shred the entire universe down to its last atom.
spoilerBio: Brought into 2023 via the Avengers' Quantum Tunnel aboard Sanctuary II, 2014 Thanos obliterated the Avengers Compound and battled Iron Man, Captain America, and Thor. In the climax of the Battle of Earth, Tony Stark wrested the six Infinity Stones from the Nano Gauntlet into his own armor and snapped his fingers, disintegrating 2014 Thanos and his entire army.
spoilerWarning: Contains climactic Battle of Earth death spoilers for Avengers: Endgame (2019)
powers: Immense superhuman strength, durability, and hand-to-hand combat mastery
Master tactical commander

name: Nebula (2014 Variant)
tagline: Thanos-loyal 2014 Nebula who infiltrated the Avengers Compound to summon Sanctuary II
biography: Still fiercely loyal to Thanos and bitter toward Gamora in 2014, this Nebula variant was captured by her father when her cybernetic memory cloud entangled with 2023 Nebula's Time Heist feed. Taking her future self's gold head-plate and Pym Particles, 2014 Nebula infiltrated the 2023 Avengers Compound undetected to open the Quantum Tunnel for Thanos's flagship.
spoilerBio: During the Battle of Earth in Endgame, 2014 Nebula attempted to retrieve the Nano Gauntlet from Hawkeye and 2014 Gamora. Confronted by her redeemed 2023 counterpart, 2014 Nebula refused to stand down and drew her weapon, forcing 2023 Nebula to shoot and kill her.
spoilerWarning: Contains character death spoilers for Avengers: Endgame (2019)
powers: Cybernetic strength, durability, and combat conditioning
Cybernetic memory network synchronization

name: Mister Fantastic (Earth-828)
tagline: Earth-828's visionary scientific pioneer and leader of the retro-futuristic Fantastic Four
biography: On the retro-futuristic 1960s world of Earth-828, brilliant scientist Reed Richards transformed global society through space-age breakthroughs alongside his wife Sue Storm, brother-in-law Johnny Storm, and best friend Ben Grimm. Four years after cosmic radiation granted him hyper-elasticity, Reed led the Fantastic Four as celebrated protectors when Galactus targeted their planet.
spoilerBio: Facing Galactus's demand to surrender his newborn son Franklin in exchange for sparing Earth-828, Reed engineered a massive planetary teleportation bridge to move Earth out of Galactus's path, before ultimately working with Sue and the team to banish the Devourer of Worlds through a cosmic portal.
spoilerWarning: Contains family and ending plot spoilers for The Fantastic Four: First Steps (2025)
powers: Hyper-elasticity and extreme bodily stretching
Genius-level theoretical physics, aerospace engineering, and robotics
equipment: Baxter Building laboratory and H.E.R.B.I.E. assistant

sources.title: Marvel.com The Fantastic Four: First Steps

name: Invisible Woman (Earth-828)
tagline: Earth-828's diplomat, co-leader of the Fantastic Four, and fierce protector of her family
biography: A respected global diplomat and co-founder of Earth-828's Fantastic Four, Sue Storm used her light-bending invisibility and formidable psionic force fields to unite nations and safeguard humanity. Expecting her first child with Reed Richards, Sue stood at the emotional and tactical heart of the team when Shalla-Bal heralded Galactus's arrival.
spoilerBio: After giving birth to Franklin Richards in deep space while escaping Galactus's ship, Sue refused to surrender her son. In the climax on Earth-828, she pushed her force-field powers to their absolute limit to drive Galactus into the teleportation portal, temporarily dying from exertion before Franklin's latent cosmic power revived her.
spoilerWarning: Contains major family and ending spoilers for The Fantastic Four: First Steps (2025)
powers: Light-bending invisibility
High-strength psionic force-field projection and telekinetic shields

sources.title: Marvel.com The Fantastic Four: First Steps

name: Human Torch (Earth-828)
tagline: Charismatic flame-wielding flyer of Earth-828's Fantastic Four
biography: Sue Storm's adventurous younger brother and the high-flying Human Torch of Earth-828, Johnny Storm mastered engulfing himself in thermal plasma for supersonic flight and pyrokinetic combat. Beneath his playful celebrity persona, Johnny proved fiercely resourceful, decoding alien transmissions during the Silver Surfer crisis.
spoilerBio: Having deciphered Shalla-Bal's Zenn-La language from space recordings, Johnny confronted the Silver Surfer with the names of the worlds she had doomed, awakening her remorse so she ultimately sacrificed herself to push Galactus through the final portal.
spoilerWarning: Contains climax spoilers for The Fantastic Four: First Steps (2025)
powers: Full-body thermal plasma ignition ('Flame On')
Supersonic flight and pyrokinetic blast projection

sources.title: Marvel.com The Fantastic Four: First Steps

name: The Thing (Earth-828)
tagline: Beloved rock-armored pilot and powerhouse of Earth-828's Fantastic Four
biography: A seasoned astronaut, pilot, and Reed Richards's loyal lifelong friend, Ben Grimm was permanently transformed by cosmic rays into the orange-rock-plated Thing. Celebrated on the streets of Earth-828's New York for his warmth and humor, Ben serves as the team's heavy hitter and chief spacecraft pilot.
spoilerBio: During the final defense of Earth-828, Ben piloted the Excelsior and teamed with Johnny and Reed to topple structural supports and drive Galactus toward the dimensional teleportation bridge.
spoilerWarning: Contains climax spoilers for The Fantastic Four: First Steps (2025)
powers: Superhuman strength and impact resistance
Rocky, virtually indestructible dermal plating
Expert spacecraft piloting

sources.title: Marvel.com The Fantastic Four: First Steps

name: Galactus
tagline: Colossal cosmic entity who devours entire planets and targeted Earth-828
biography: An ancient, titanic cosmic being aboard an immense world-ship, Galactus sustains his endless hunger by consuming inhabited planets across the cosmos. Dispatched by his herald Shalla-Bal, Galactus descended toward Earth-828, confronting the Fantastic Four with a terrifying ultimatum.
spoilerBio: Sensing immense cosmic power inside Reed and Sue's unborn child Franklin, Galactus offered to spare Earth-828 if they surrendered the infant to replace him as the cosmos's vessel. When they refused, Galactus marched into New York, only to be shoved through a planetary teleportation portal into deep space by Sue Storm and Shalla-Bal.
spoilerWarning: Contains major plot and ending spoilers for The Fantastic Four: First Steps (2025)
powers: Colossal cosmic size, strength, and near-invulnerability
Power Cosmic manipulation and world-ship energy projection
equipment: World-consuming cosmic armor and starship Taa II

sources.title: Marvel.com The Fantastic Four: First Steps

name: Silver Surfer (Shalla-Bal)
tagline: Silver-skinned herald of Galactus who spared her homeworld of Zenn-La by serving as his scout
biography: A scientist from Zenn-La who volunteered to become Galactus's herald in exchange for sparing her own planet, Shalla-Bal was transformed into the Silver Surfer and granted a fraction of the Power Cosmic. Arriving on Earth-828 atop her silver board, she announced the planet's impending consumption.
spoilerBio: After Johnny Storm confronted her with recordings of the millions of lives lost on worlds she had marked, Shalla-Bal turned against her master during the New York climax, propelling herself into Galactus to shove him into the dimensional portal and sacrificing herself in the process.
spoilerWarning: Contains sacrifice and ending spoilers for The Fantastic Four: First Steps (2025)
powers: Power Cosmic energy projection and matter phasing
Faster-than-light interstellar flight via silver surfboard

sources.title: Marvel.com The Fantastic Four: First Steps

name: Daredevil
tagline: Blind Hell's Kitchen attorney who fights organized crime using hyper-acute radar senses
biography: Blinded in childhood after toxic waste spilled into his eyes, Matt Murdock developed superhuman hearing, touch, and a sonar-like radar sense. Following his boxer father Jack Murdock's murder by mobsters, Matt became a pro bono Hell's Kitchen defense lawyer by day and the crimson-clad vigilante Daredevil by night.
spoilerBio: After Bullseye murdered Elektra and her father, Daredevil confronted Wilson Fisk in his penthouse, exposing Fisk as the Kingpin and defeating him in hand-to-hand combat while sparing his life for the police.
spoilerWarning: Contains climax spoilers for Daredevil (2003)
powers: Hyper-acute hearing, smell, and sonar-like radar sense
Peak acrobatic martial arts mastery
equipment: Two-piece interlocking billy club / grappling cane

name: Elektra
tagline: Twin-sai martial artist resurrected by Stick who later joined the Void resistance
biography: Daughter of Greek billionaire Nikolas Natchios, Elektra trained extensively in martial arts before crossing paths with Matt Murdock in New York. After Bullseye murdered her father and fatally impaled her in Daredevil (2003), Elektra was resurrected by the blind master Stick and became an elite contract assassin.
spoilerBio: In Elektra (2005), she defied the Hand by protecting targets Mark and Abby Miller, slaying Kirigi in her childhood home. Years later, pruned into the Void in Deadpool & Wolverine (2024), Elektra fought alongside Blade, Gambit, and X-23 to help Deadpool and Wolverine overthrow Cassandra Nova.
spoilerWarning: Contains resurrection and crossover spoilers for Daredevil (2003), Elektra (2005), and Deadpool & Wolverine (2024)
powers: Master ninjutsu, acrobatics, and twin-sai combat
Kimagure precognitive awareness (taught by Stick)

name: Kingpin
tagline: Imposing New York crime syndicate boss who ordered Jack Murdock's and Nikolas Natchios's murders
biography: A physically colossal criminal mastermind posing as a legitimate New York philanthropist, Wilson Fisk ruled the city's underworld as the Kingpin. Years after personally beating boxer Jack Murdock to death as a mob enforcer, Fisk hired Bullseye to assassinate Nikolas Natchios, drawing the wrath of Daredevil.
spoilerBio: When Daredevil infiltrated Fisk's penthouse and used breaking sprinklers to visualize his towering frame, Fisk was overpowered, unmasked Matt Murdock, and was left in police custody vowing retribution.
spoilerWarning: Contains ending spoilers for Daredevil (2003)
powers: Colossal physical strength and brute-force brawling

name: Bullseye
tagline: Sadistic Irish contract killer with flawless projectile accuracy hired by Kingpin
biography: A tattooed, trench-coat-wearing assassin obsessed with never missing a target, Bullseye could kill effortlessly with paperclips, peanuts, playing cards, or shards of glass. Hired by Wilson Fisk to eliminate Nikolas Natchios, Bullseye framed Daredevil for the murder and pursued Elektra into St. Patrick's Cathedral.
spoilerBio: After fatally stabbing Elektra with her own sai inside the cathedral, Bullseye dueled Daredevil atop the pipe organ, where Daredevil manipulated a sniper's bullet to pierce both of Bullseye's hands before throwing him through a stained-glass window.
spoilerWarning: Contains climax spoilers for Daredevil (2003)
powers: Infallible projectile aim with any improvised object
equipment: Throwing stars, daggers, and improvised projectiles

name: Stick
tagline: Blind Chaste grandmaster who resurrected Elektra and trained her in Kimagure
biography: Leader of the virtuous Chaste order opposing the Hand, the blind martial arts master Stick resurrected Elektra Natchios after her death in New York and trained her in sensory mastery and the ancient Kimagure technique. Though he dismissed Elektra when her inner rage proved too volatile, he secretly arranged her final redemption test.
spoilerBio: Stick revealed that he had hired Elektra to assassinate Mark and Abby Miller specifically so she would choose to protect Abby—the next 'Treasure' sought by the Hand—proving her heart remained pure.
spoilerWarning: Contains ending plot twist spoilers for Elektra (2005)
powers: Grandmaster bo-staff combat and Kimagure resurrection mastery
Heightened blind sensory awareness

name: Ghost Rider
tagline: Daredevil stunt motorcyclist bound by Mephistopheles's pact to ride as the flaming Spirit of Vengeance
biography: To save his dying father Barton Blaze from cancer, young stunt motorcyclist Johnny Blaze signed a pact in blood with Mephistopheles—only for his father to die the next day in a stunt crash. Years later, Mephistopheles activated the contract, transforming Johnny by night into the hellfire-wreathed Ghost Rider to hunt rogue demons.
spoilerBio: After defeating Blackheart in Ghost Rider (2007), Johnny refused Mephistopheles's offer to return his soul, choosing to keep the curse to fight evil. In the soft-rebooted sequel Spirit of Vengeance (2012), Blaze exiled himself to Eastern Europe before rescuing young Danny Ketch from Roarke, purging the dark side of Zarathos to wield angelic blue hellfire.
spoilerWarning: Contains ending spoilers for Ghost Rider (2007) and Spirit of Vengeance (2012)
powers: Hellfire manipulation and Penance Stare
Superhuman strength, durability, and demonic vehicle possession

name: Blackheart
tagline: Rebellious demonic son of Mephistopheles seeking the Contract of San Venganza
biography: Straying from his father Mephistopheles's rule, the fallen demon Blackheart arrived on Earth alongside three elemental allies—Abigor, Gressil, and Wallow—to locate the ancient Contract of San Venganza. Commanding a touch that decays mortal flesh, Blackheart sought to absorb a thousand damned souls and overthrow Hell.
spoilerBio: After absorbing the souls of San Venganza to become 'Legion', Blackheart overwhelmed Ghost Rider in daylight until Roxanne tossed Johnny a shotgun—empowering Ghost Rider in the shadows to burn away Blackheart's stolen souls with the Penance Stare.
spoilerWarning: Contains climax spoilers for Ghost Rider (2007)
powers: Lethal necrotic touch and shadow teleportation
Absorption of damned souls ('Legion' form)

name: Mephistopheles
tagline: Silver-tongued Lord of Hell who tricked Johnny Blaze into becoming his bounty hunter
biography: Posing as a sharp-suited stranger, the Devil Mephistopheles coerced seventeen-year-old Johnny Blaze into trading his soul to cure his father's cancer, only to orchestrate Barton Blaze's fatal stunt accident the next day. Decades later, Mephistopheles activated Johnny's Ghost Rider curse to hunt down his rebellious son Blackheart.
spoilerBio: Following Blackheart's defeat, Mephistopheles offered to release Johnny from the Ghost Rider curse, only for Johnny to refuse—vowing to turn the Devil's own power against him.
spoilerWarning: Contains ending spoilers for Ghost Rider (2007)
powers: Soul-contract magic, demonic immortality, and time-freezing presence

name: Roxanne Simpson
tagline: Investigative reporter and Johnny Blaze's lost love drawn into the Ghost Rider's supernatural war
biography: Separated from Johnny Blaze when he abruptly fled town after his father's death, Roxanne Simpson became a respected television reporter in Texas. Reunited with Johnny during an interview assignment, she uncovered the truth behind his demonic transformation and was targeted by Blackheart to force Blaze's compliance.
spoilerBio: Held captive in San Venganza, Roxanne helped tip the final battle by tossing Carter Slade's shotgun to Johnny, enabling Ghost Rider to defeat Blackheart before bidding Johnny a bittersweet farewell.
spoilerWarning: Contains climax spoilers for Ghost Rider (2007)
powers: Investigative journalism and resourcefulness under crisis

name: The Punisher (2004)
tagline: Former Delta Force & FBI agent waging psychological and tactical war on Howard Saint's empire
biography: A decorated Delta Force veteran and undercover FBI agent retiring after one final sting operation, Frank Castle watched his wife Maria, son Will, and entire extended family massacred in Puerto Rico on Howard Saint's orders. Surviving a gunshot to the chest, Castle shed his former life to become the skull-chested Punisher.
spoilerBio: Rather than merely shooting Saint, Castle systematically manipulated Saint's paranoia—tricking him into executing his own best friend Quentin Glass and his wife Livia—before killing Saint in an explosive car-lot ambush and choosing to continue his vigilante war.
spoilerWarning: Contains ending spoilers for The Punisher (2004)
powers: Delta Force & FBI tactical combat, marksmanship, and explosives mastery
Psychological warfare and counter-intelligence

name: Howard Saint
tagline: Vindictive Tampa crime boss and money launderer whose order to kill Castle's family sealed his doom
biography: A wealthy Tampa money launderer and club owner operating behind a polished socialite facade, Howard Saint lost his favorite son Bobby during an FBI arms sting led by Frank Castle. Driven by grief and his wife Livia's demand for total vengeance, Saint ordered the slaughter of Castle's entire family reunion.
spoilerBio: Blinded by Castle's planted evidence, Saint murdered his loyal lieutenant Quentin Glass and had his wife Livia thrown onto train tracks before Castle revealed the deception and strapped Saint to an exploding line of rigged cars.
spoilerWarning: Contains climax spoilers for The Punisher (2004)
powers: Criminal syndicate wealth and ruthless underworld influence

name: The Punisher (War Zone)
tagline: Relentless one-man army in New York's War Zone facing Jigsaw and Loony Bin Jim
biography: In Lionsgate's standalone 2008 reboot, former Force Recon Marine Frank Castle has waged a brutal five-year war against New York's Mafia families after his wife and children were caught in a mob crossfire. Operating out of abandoned safehouses with armorer Microchip, Castle relentlessly hunts down every crime syndicate in the city.
spoilerBio: After accidentally killing an undercover FBI agent during a raid on mobster Billy Russoti, Castle nearly retired—until Jigsaw kidnapped the slain agent's widow and daughter, prompting Castle to storm the Bradstreet Hotel, execute Loony Bin Jim, and burn Jigsaw alive.
spoilerWarning: Contains climax spoilers for Punisher: War Zone (2008)
powers: Force Recon heavy-weapons mastery and relentless close-quarters lethality
equipment: Heavy ordnance, grenade launchers, and combat knives

name: Jigsaw
tagline: Sadistic mobster horribly scarred by glass-crushing machinery who united New York's gangs against Castle
biography: Once a vain, flamboyant Mafia enforcer known as 'Billy The Beaut', Billy Russoti fell into an industrial glass-crushing vat when the Punisher raided his recycling plant. Surviving reconstructive surgery with a twisted, patchwork face, Russoti renamed himself Jigsaw and freed his psychotic brother Loony Bin Jim to destroy Frank Castle.
spoilerBio: After killing Microchip and seizing hostages at the Bradstreet Hotel, Jigsaw watched Castle kill his brother before Castle impaled Jigsaw on a spike and hurled him into a roaring fire.
spoilerWarning: Contains climax spoilers for Punisher: War Zone (2008)
powers: Criminal leadership and extreme pain tolerance

name: The Punisher (1989)
tagline: Presumed-dead police veteran waging a five-year subterranean war against the Mafia and Yakuza
biography: A decorated police officer presumed killed in the car bombing that murdered his wife and two daughters, Frank Castle retreated into the city sewers for five years, executing 125 mobsters as the Punisher. When Lady Tanaka's Yakuza kidnapped Mafia bosses' children to seize control of organized crime, Castle forged a reluctant truce to rescue the hostages.
spoilerBio: Infiltrating Lady Tanaka's headquarters alongside mob boss Gianni Franco, Castle slayed the Yakuza leadership—and when Franco betrayed him immediately afterward, Castle shot Franco dead before vanishing back into the shadows.
spoilerWarning: Contains ending spoilers for The Punisher (1989)
powers: Elite police tactical combat, martial arts, and weapons proficiency
equipment: Skull-hilted combat knives and submachine guns
